title: Home
text:
Welcome to my portfolio website. I am an ecosystem scientist currently pursuing a Professional Science Master’s in Ecosystem Science and Sustainability at Colorado State University, with a focus on carbon management.
My background combines sustainability research, environmental data analysis, and geospatial science. I am especially interested in understanding carbon emissions, climate change, and how data can support better environmental decisions.




I work at the intersection of ecology, data science, and sustainability. My experience includes:

Environmental data analysis using R

Geospatial analysis and mapping using ArcGIS Pro

Statistical analysis and basic machine learning

Qualitative research and coding using MaxQDA

Science communication in sustainability and climate topics

Working in both English and Arabic






Conducted research on public perceptions of bat research facilities.
Contributing researcher and co-author at KAUST on a chapter on the evolution of the UNFCCC and global carbon governance

Developed a StoryMap user guide for Namibia’s environmental tracking platform in collaboration with CNHP and the University of Namibia,

Worked on projects analyzing carbon emissions and environmental data using statistical and machine learning methods.





Some of the projects included in this portfolio:

Namibia StoryMap User Guide

Carbon Emissions Analysis During COVID-19

Wolverine Habitat Suitability GIS Model

You can explore more details in the Projects section.




I am interested in working in carbon management and sustainability, especially in roles that combine environmental science, data analysis, and policy. My goal is to contribute to solutions that reduce emissions and support sustainable systems.

title: Projects
text:
Namibia StoryMap User Guide
For my sustainability capstone project, I worked on a StoryMap user guide for an interactive biodiversity platform in Namibia. This project was developed in collaboration with the Colorado Natural Heritage Program (CNHP) and the University of Namibia.
My role focused on explaining how users can navigate the interactive map, use tools such as measuring distance and area, turn layers on and off, and understand biodiversity indicators.

title: Projects
section: Carbon Emissions and Energy Use During COVID-19
text:
Carbon Emissions and Energy Use During COVID-19
In this project, I analyzed changes in greenhouse gas emissions in the top five emitting countries (China, United States, India, Russia, and Japan) from 2015 to 2022.
I used statistical methods such as ANOVA and regression, along with machine learning models like random forest. The results showed that emissions dropped during COVID-19 but rebounded afterward, and gas emissions were a strong predictor.
Project Website

title: Projects
text:
Wolverine Habitat Suitability Analysis
This project focused on identifying suitable habitats for wolverines in Clear Creek County, Colorado using GIS analysis. I used elevation, snowpack, and distance from roads to model habitat suitability.
The results showed that suitable habitats are mostly located in high-elevation areas with low human disturbance.

title: Publications
text:
“Not in my backyard”: Online narratives of societal perceptions and skepticism towards emerging infectious disease research

Co-author and contributing researcher

This research examines how the public discusses and perceives emerging infectious disease research, with a focus on online narratives, trust, and skepticism.



UNFCCC and Global Carbon Governance

Contributing researcher and co-author at KAUST on a chapter examining the evolution of the UNFCCC and global carbon governance

This work focuses on understanding how international climate agreements have evolved and how they influence global carbon management and policy.
